clue.text: What computer operators may do today in warships

definitions.text: What computer operators may do today
definitions.meaning: on 1 January 2000 computer staff feared the zeros of the new date (the millennium bug)
big-gunned battleships of the early twentieth century, named after HMS Dreadnought

explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 1 January 2000, when the 'millennium bug' threatened computers that stored years as two digits ending in noughts.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreadnoughts were the heavily armed battleships that followed HMS Dreadnought of 1906.

clue.text: Tramp in possession of one set of papers

indicators.note: in possession of says the first piece holds the next

parts.note: a dosser is a vagrant who sleeps rough
I is one in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A vagrant is carrying a bundle of documents.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a collection of documents about a person or subject.

clue.text: Police finally getting armour and communication system for PCs

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of police

parts.note: mail is armour of linked metal rings

explanation.surface: Police officers finally get body armour and a new radio network.
explanation.walkthrough: 'PCs' looks like police constables, but means personal computers.
explanation.definitionFit: Electronic mail is the messaging system run between computers.

clue.text: Campaign to save forests etc, being potentially turned into matchwood

indicators.note: potentially turned into says the letters of the last word could be rearranged to make the answer

explanation.surface: Green campaigners act because trees might end up as matchwood.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue runs backwards: the answer is the anagram that matchwood could be turned into.
explanation.definitionFit: Doomwatch means environmental vigilance against ecological disaster, after a 1970s BBC series.

clue.text: Empty graves in Rome, for example, upsetting nobody there

definitions.text: Empty graves in Rome, for example

indicators.note: upsetting in a down clue means the word is turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: nemo is Latin, the language of Rome, for nobody

explanation.surface: Vandals in Rome empty the graves and nobody minds.
explanation.walkthrough: In Hamlet, before Julius Caesar fell 'the graves stood tenantless', a portent of doom; 'there' points to Rome for the Latin NEMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenantless graves were a portent before Caesar's death, a sign of things to come.

clue.text: Boy who's young relative to four?

definitions.text: Boy who's young relative to four?

parts.words: Boy who's young relative to four?
parts.note: everyone has four grandparents, so a lad is the junior kin of four people at once

explanation.definitionFit: A son's son is the young male relative of his four grandparents.

clue.text: Furthermore, this unit's involved in uproar

indicators.note: involved in says one word sits inside another, so taking the outer word away leaves the inner one

parts.note: a furore is an uproar

explanation.surface: Moreover, this measure is caught up in a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Furthermore is FURORE with the answer involved in it, so removing FURORE leaves a unit of heat.
explanation.definitionFit: A therm is a unit of heat used in billing for gas.

clue.text: A container in the best metal

indicators.note: in says the next pieces go inside

parts.note: a plum is the best of something, as in a plum job
a tin is a container

explanation.surface: A box placed among the finest metals.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum is a precious silvery metallic element.

clue.text: Unsuitable situation for outpost, you might say

definitions.text: Unsuitable situation for outpost, you might say

parts.words: Unsuitable situation for outpost, you might say
parts.note: outpost read as out-post, outgoing letters, which do not belong in the office tray for incoming mail

explanation.definitionFit: An office tray for incoming documents is the wrong place for outgoing mail.

clue.text: Accordingly, a popular time for TV programme

parts.note: so means accordingly, therefore
pop is short for popular
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster explains that a TV programme was scheduled at a time when most people watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial drama on television, originally sponsored by soap makers.

clue.text: Woman said to provide cover for M?

indicators.note: said signals that the letters are spoken rather than written

parts.note: in the alphabet L and N stand either side of M, covering it

explanation.surface: A woman is apparently going to stand in for M, the spymaster.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud, 'L 'n'' (L and N, the letters flanking M) is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a female given name.

clue.text: Relative gains resulting from union negotiations

definitions.text: Relative gains resulting from union negotiations

parts.words: Relative gains resulting from union negotiations
parts.note: looks like trade-union pay gains, but the union is a marriage and the gains are relatives acquired through it

explanation.definitionFit: Relatives by marriage are acquired when one weds, so they are family gained through a union.

clue.text: Tore madly round new tourist attraction-that shows how far an American goes

definitions.text: that shows how far an American goes

indicators.note: round says the rearranged letters go around the next piece
madly says the letters of tore are wildly rearranged

parts.note: the Millennium Dome in Greenwich opened in London at the start of 2000

explanation.surface: Someone rushes round a newly opened sight, and an American device records the distance.
explanation.walkthrough: The Millennium Dome at Greenwich was London's brand-new attraction when this puzzle ran on 1 January 2000; 'American' marks the definition as the US name for a mileometer.
explanation.definitionFit: An odometer is the instrument recording distance travelled, the usual American term for a mileometer.

clue.text: Discount on pet

parts.note: re means on, concerning
a pet is a fit of sulking, and bate is British slang for a temper

explanation.surface: A price reduction offered on a pet animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal but means a sulk; BATE, as in 'in a bate', is a British word for a bad temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebate is a partial refund or deduction from a sum owed.

clue.text: Frightful things a possible problem now produces

parts.note: the millennium bug was the feared computer problem of 1 January 2000
bears means produces, as a tree bears fruit

explanation.surface: Scary things come from an issue that might strike right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugbears are objects of dread, originally bogeymen.

clue.text: Greedily grab a lot over a recent time of celebration

parts.note: to hog is to take more than one's share

indicators.note: over says the first piece covers, and so holds, the next

parts.note: many means a lot

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs themselves at a party just past.
explanation.walkthrough: HOGMANAY is the Scottish New Year's Eve celebration, which had just happened when this puzzle appeared on 1 January.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish festivities of 31 December, just past on the publication date.

clue.text: Computer showing Whistler's mother, for example?

definitions.meaning: Whistler's famous portrait of his mother shows a ma in a frame

explanation.definitionFit: A mainframe is a large central computer; split, it is a mother pictured in a frame.

clue.text: A relatively extended 'dispute

parts.note: relatively means involving relatives, so the dispute extends across families and generations

explanation.definitionFit: A vendetta is a blood feud carried on between families.

clue.text: American VIP, one put up in London last year

definitions.meaning: US slang for an important person

definitions.text: one put up in London last year
definitions.meaning: the London Eye, a giant observation ferris wheel, was erected on the Thames in 1999

explanation.definitionFit: A bigwig is called a big wheel in America; the London Eye is a huge fairground-style ride.

clue.text: Less successful financial dealer?

definitions.meaning: an agent who buys and sells for clients

explanation.definitionFit: A broker trades stocks for clients; as a comparative it means poorer.

clue.text: Buy it around 2000, right? That's not so clever

indicators.note: around says the first piece goes round the next

parts.note: to buy it is slang for to die
MM is 2000 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A shopper is urged to purchase something at about the millennium, and someone remarks it was unwise.
explanation.definitionFit: Dimmer is the comparative of dim, meaning stupid, so less bright.

clue.text: Person no longer working on Scottish island

parts.note: re means on, concerning
Tiree is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone who has stopped work goes to live on a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: A retiree is someone who has retired from employment.

clue.text: Take power into one's own hands and cover up?

definitions.text: Take power into one's own hands

parts.note: over describes something lying on top, covering
in horse racing a jockey who is up is riding

explanation.surface: A rebel seizes control and then hides the evidence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' is a racing term: 'with Dettori up' means Dettori is riding.
explanation.definitionFit: To override is to overrule others and act on one's own authority.

clue.text: This we can refer to a single top person

definitions.text: This we can refer to a single top person

parts.words: This we can refer to a single top person
parts.note: the plural we used by a monarch speaking of herself alone

explanation.definitionFit: The royal we is the plural pronoun a sovereign uses for herself.

clue.text: Compensation, being shot? On the contrary

indicators.note: on the contrary says the two parts of that phrase swap round

parts.note: a gun being shot is set off

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether being shot earns compensation, then corrects themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' moves SET from the front of SETOFF to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An offset is something that balances or counteracts a loss.

clue.text: Outrageous points raised in argument

indicators.note: raised in a down clue says the pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OTT, over the top, means outrageous
E and S, east and south, are compass points

explanation.surface: Extreme views are put forward in a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns OTTES upwards to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-to is a fight or heated argument.

clue.text: Form forum so lacking in class?

definitions.meaning: the word form is forum with no U
not upper-class, in Nancy Mitford's U and ... usage

explanation.walkthrough: U meant upper-class in 1950s British usage; non-U words marked the speaker as lower-class.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-U describes speech or manners not considered upper-class.

clue.text: In New Year, lunacy's beginning too soon

indicators.note: in says the next piece goes inside the rearranged letters
new says the letters of year are made into a fresh arrangement
beginning picks the first letter of lunacy

explanation.surface: At New Year a bout of madness begins before its time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' turns YEAR into EARY; 'In' puts L inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected or proper time.

clue.text: In 2000, plant producing sailing vessel

parts.note: two M, M being the Roman numeral for a thousand
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A ship was launched in the year 2000.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-master is a ship with two masts, such as a schooner or brig.

clue.text: Contemporary revival of Mongolian architecture?

parts.note: Coleridge's Kubla Khan, the Mongol emperor; the new Millennium Dome is cast as its modern revival

explanation.walkthrough: In Coleridge's poem 'In Xanadu did Kubla Khan a stately pleasure-dome decree'; the Millennium Dome opened as this puzzle ran.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Coleridge's poem about the Mongol ruler's palace of delights.
